content:
Mammut started life in 1862 as a small Swiss ropery, and that mountain-safety habit still shapes its jackets, packs and boots today. For Kenyan hikers, Mammut is a strong pick for wet forest days and cold summit nights, especially when you find a good thrifted piece in Nairobi at a fraction of the new price.

The trouble is that Mammut labels are full of codes like HS, SO and ML, and a second-hand jacket rarely comes with a shop assistant to explain them. Below you will find what the brand is known for, which of its lines suit trails from Ngong Hills to Point Lenana, how the sizing runs, what to check on a used item, and where to look for it in Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Origin: Mammut was founded in 1862 by Kaspar Tanner as a rope maker in Dintikon, Switzerland, and is now based in Seon.
  • Known for: climbing ropes, harnesses and avalanche gear, plus hiking jackets, backpacks and boots.
  • Label codes: HS means hardshell (waterproof), SO means softshell, IN means insulated and ML means mid layer.
  • Waterproofing: Mammut uses its own DRYtechnology membranes on many shells and GORE-TEX on others.
  • Best Kenyan uses: Aberdares and Mt Kenya forest rain, windy ridges and summit nights near 4,985 m.
  • Buying tip: thrifted Mammut in Nairobi is good value, but check seams, zips and the membrane before you pay.

What Is Mammut Known For?

Mammut is a Swiss mountain brand best known for climbing ropes and safety equipment, and it applies the same engineering to hiking jackets, packs and footwear. The mammoth logo arrived in 1943, when the company started selling under the Mammut name.

The rope heritage matters more than you might think. A firm that has spent over 160 years making gear that holds a falling climber tends to obsess over abrasion, stitching and how fabric moves with the body. That shows up in small details: hoods that fit over a helmet, pockets placed above a hip belt, and two-way zips on shells meant for people wearing a harness.

Today the range covers outdoor clothing, backpacks, sleeping bags, ropes, harnesses and the Barryvox avalanche transceiver. Climbing equipment still makes up roughly a third of sales, so this is not a fashion label borrowing mountain imagery. Its hiking kit sits beside technical gear designed for the Alps, which is why the better pieces handle a sleet-soaked night on Mt Kenya without complaint.

How does Mammut compare with other big outdoor brands?

Mammut sits at the technical, premium end of the outdoor market, and its cut is usually trim and athletic. If you are comparing it with the jackets covered in our guides to Jack Wolfskin shells and Berghaus waterproofs, expect a closer fit and fewer casual styles. For a wider view of how the big names stack up, see our hub on hiking boot brands.

Which Mammut Gear Suits Kenyan Trails?

For most Kenyan hikers, the most useful Mammut pieces are a hardshell rain jacket, a softshell for wind, a fleece mid layer and a 20-30 litre daypack. The boots suit longer, rockier routes. Climbing gear is specialist and only matters if you rope up on Batian or Nelion.

Mammut hardshell jackets (HS) for the rains

A jacket with HS on the label is a fully waterproof shell. Many use the brand's own DRYtechnology membrane; the Mammut Outdoor HS Hooded Jacket, for example, is built from a stretch three-layer DRYtechnology Pro fabric the brand describes as PFC-free, with backpack-compatible front pockets, a helmet-compatible hood with a stiffened peak and a two-way front zip. Other models use GORE-TEX, which the label will state clearly.

In Kenya, an HS jacket earns its keep during the long rains from March to May and the short rains from October to December. On the Kinangop side of the Aberdares, afternoon downpours can soak a cotton hoodie in minutes. A three-layer shell also blocks the wind that rips across the Ngong Hills ridge, so it is worth packing even on dry days.

Mammut softshells (SO) for wind and drizzle

A softshell marked SO stretches, breathes and shrugs off wind and light drizzle, but it is not a storm shell. The Ultimate VIII SO, one of the brand's long-running softshells, uses a three-layer GORE-TEX WINDSTOPPER build and weighs about 503 g, according to its retail listing. That makes it a good outer layer for a cold, breezy start up Mt Longonot or a misty morning at Elephant Hill.

The catch: in a real Aberdares downpour, a softshell will eventually wet through. Pair it with a light rain shell or a poncho in your pack during the rainy months.

Mammut fleece and insulated layers (ML and IN)

ML on the label means a mid layer, usually fleece, while IN means insulation such as down or synthetic fill. An ML fleece is the workhorse for Kenyan hiking: warm enough for 6 am starts at Table Mountain, light enough to stuff in a daypack by 10 am. Save the IN jackets for camp evenings and summit nights on Mt Kenya, where temperatures regularly drop below freezing. Our guide to layering for cold weather hikes explains how the layers work together.

Mammut backpacks for day hikes

The Lithium series is the line most day hikers meet. The Lithium 20 we looked at holds 20 litres, weighs about 710 g, and has a Contact U-frame back system, a detachable padded hip belt, a sleeve for a hydration bladder, a built-in detachable rain cover and a trekking pole holder. The fabric is polyamide with a PFC-free water-repellent finish.

That spec list fits a typical Kenyan day hike almost perfectly. Twenty litres carries three litres of water, a rain shell, a fleece and lunch for Oldoinyo Lesatima. The integrated rain cover is the feature people forget to check on a used pack, so pull it out and make sure it is still attached and untorn. If you need something larger, our guide to choosing hiking backpacks in Nairobi walks through sizes from 20 to 70 litres.

Mammut hiking boots

The Ducan II High GTX is a good example of the brand's approach to boots. It has a GORE-TEX lining, a Vibram outsole and the Flextron system, a spring-steel insert in the sole meant to add stability and energy return. The brand pitches it for anything from short hikes to multi-day tours.

A boot like that suits Mt Kenya's Sirimon and Chogoria routes, Elephant Hill's bamboo mud and the scree near Point Lenana. For easy dry trails like Karura Forest, it is more boot than you need.

Is Mammut Worth the Money for Hiking in Kenya?

New gear from this brand is expensive, so it makes the most sense for people who hike monthly or plan big mountains. Bought thrifted, it becomes far easier to justify: a good second-hand hardshell can cost a fraction of a new one and still has years of use left.

Think about how often you hike and where. A beginner doing Ngong Hills twice a year will not notice much difference between a Mammut shell and a cheaper waterproof. Someone training for Mt Kenya, or hiking the Aberdares through the rains, will feel the difference in breathability, fit over layers and how the hood stays put in wind.

When is cheaper gear the better choice?

Cheaper gear wins when you are still working out whether you enjoy hiking, or when the item wears out quickly anyway. Socks, gloves and a basic rain poncho do not need a premium badge. Put the money into the pieces that protect you most in bad weather: the shell jacket, the boots and the pack that carries everything.

How Does Mammut Sizing Fit?

Mammut clothing generally runs trim and athletic, with longer arms built for climbing. Many hikers go up one size if they plan to wear a fleece under a hardshell. Footwear follows Mondo sizing, where each full size equals 1 cm of foot length.

The European cut catches people out. A medium is often closer to a snug fit than a relaxed one, which is great for movement on a scramble but tight over a thick fleece. When you try a jacket, put on the layer you would actually wear underneath, raise both arms above your head and check that the hem does not ride up past your waist and the cuffs still cover your wrists.

Mammut boot sizes and UK conversions

Footwear is where conversions matter most. One UK retailer's fit guide notes that the brand's UK sizes run about half a size large, so someone who normally takes a UK 8 may fit a UK 7.5 in this brand, while its EU sizes run slightly small. The safest method is to measure your foot in centimetres, standing, in the evening, and match that to the Mondo size printed inside the tongue.

On a thrifted pair, the Mondo number is your best friend because it ignores the confusing UK, EU and US columns. Leave about a thumb's width in front of your longest toe for steep descents like Longonot's crater path.

Buying Second-Hand Mammut: What to Check

A used piece is a good buy when the membrane, seams, zips and soles are intact. Problems usually show up in the same places, so a two-minute check catches most of them before you pay.

  1. Read the inner label. Look for HS, SO, ML or IN in the name, the membrane (DRYtechnology or GORE-TEX), and the care instructions. A missing inner label makes it harder to know what you are buying.
  2. Check the seam tape. Turn a hardshell inside out and run a finger along the taped seams at the shoulders and hood. Peeling tape means leaks.
  3. Look for delamination. Bubbling or a crinkly, flaking inner surface on a shell means the membrane is failing. Skip it for rainy-season use.
  4. Test every zip. Run the main zip and both pit zips (if fitted) end to end. Sticky zips can often be cleaned, but broken sliders on a waterproof zip are costly to fix.
  5. Squeeze pack buckles and foam. On a backpack, squeeze the hip belt foam and click each buckle. Crushed foam and cracked buckles make a pack uncomfortable.
  6. Flex the boot soles. Look at lug depth on the Vibram sole and press the midsole for cracks. Check the inside heel lining for holes.

How can you tell if Mammut gear is genuine?

Genuine items have neat, even stitching, clean and consistent logo embroidery, sewn-in inner labels with care symbols and product codes, and branded zip pulls on many models. Since 2019, some collections have also carried an NFC tag sewn into the product that links to the brand's Mammut Connect app for product details and registration.

None of these signs is proof on its own, and older genuine items will not have an NFC tag. Use them together. A suspiciously perfect logo on a jacket with flimsy fabric, uneven seam tape and a vague label deserves a second look, wherever you buy it.

Caring for Mammut Gear in Kenya's Dust and Rain

Hardshells and softshells last far longer when you wash them gently, dry them fully and refresh the water-repellent finish. Red dust from trails like Lukenya and Ngong clogs fabric pores, so cleaning actually improves breathability.

Wash a hardshell with a technical cleaner, not ordinary detergent or fabric softener, on a cool, gentle cycle. Rinse twice. If the care label allows it, a short tumble on low heat helps reactivate the outer finish; otherwise hang it in the shade, because harsh equatorial sun is hard on technical fabrics over time. When water stops beading on the surface, re-proof with a spray-on DWR treatment.

For packs, empty every pocket, brush out dust and soil, rinse the hydration sleeve and dry the pack upside down. For boots, knock off mud after each hike, rinse, stuff with newspaper and dry away from direct heat. A wet GORE-TEX boot left in a car boot after an Aberdares hike is the fastest way to grow mould inside.

What should you do if a Mammut jacket starts leaking?

Start by cleaning it, since dirt and body oils often make a working membrane feel like it leaks. If the outer fabric still soaks through after washing and re-proofing, check the seam tape and look for delamination. Taped seams can sometimes be patched with seam sealer; a delaminated membrane cannot be fully repaired.

Pro Tips for Buying Mammut

  • Bring your layers: try the shell over the fleece you will hike in, because the cut is trim.
  • Match the code to the job: HS for rain, SO for wind, ML for warmth on the move, IN for camp and summits.
  • Measure feet in centimetres: use the Mondo size inside the boots instead of UK or EU numbers.
  • Check the rain cover: on a used Lithium pack, pull out the built-in cover and look for tears.
  • Look at seams in daylight: peeling tape and delamination are easier to spot by a window.
  • Re-proof after washing: a fresh DWR treatment brings back beading on an older shell.

Planning a Big Mountain in Mammut Kit

For Mt Kenya, an HS hardshell, a fleece and an insulated jacket cover the layering you need from the forest zone up to Point Lenana at 4,985 m. Add warm gloves, a hat and a 30-40 litre pack if you carry your own gear.

The forest zone on the Chogoria and Naro Moru routes can be wet and muddy, the moorlands windy and exposed, and summit mornings well below freezing. A shell with a helmet-compatible hood, like many HS jackets from the brand, seals out wind better than a loose hood once you add a beanie. Check current park rules and fees with the Kenya Wildlife Service before you go, and see our full Mt Kenya gear list for Nairobi shoppers for everything else you will pack. For details on the fabrics, the brand's Outdoor HS Hooded Jacket page lists the DRYtechnology Pro features.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Mammut a good brand for hiking?

Mammut is a well-regarded Swiss brand for hiking, founded in 1862 as a rope maker, and its jackets, packs and boots are built to mountain-safety standards. Its HS hardshells, Lithium daypacks and GORE-TEX boots handle wet forest trails and cold summits well. The main downsides are a trim European cut and a high new price, which thrifted buying helps with.

Is Mammut more expensive than The North Face?

Mammut and The North Face both sit in the premium bracket, and Mammut's technical alpine lines are usually priced near the top of it. Exact prices vary by model and country. In Kenya, the easiest way to own either brand affordably is second-hand, where condition matters far more than the original price tag. Our guide to The North Face in Nairobi covers that brand in detail.

Does Mammut run small?

Mammut clothing tends to feel snug because of its trim, athletic European cut, so many hikers size up one when planning to layer underneath. For footwear, the brand uses Mondo sizing in centimetres; one UK retailer notes Mammut's UK sizes run about half a size large. Measure your feet, try jackets over a fleece, and check arm length with your arms raised.

What does HS mean on a Mammut jacket?

HS on a Mammut jacket stands for hardshell, meaning a fully waterproof and windproof outer layer with taped seams. The brand also uses SO for softshell, ML for mid layer (usually fleece) and IN for insulated jackets. In Kenya, an HS jacket is the one to pack for the long rains, the short rains and any Mt Kenya or Aberdares hike.

Can I buy Mammut gear in Nairobi?

Mammut gear can be found in Nairobi mainly through second-hand and thrifted outdoor shops, including our shop at Mountain Mall on Thika Road. Stock of big brands changes often, so a specific jacket, pack or boot may come and go within days. Message us on WhatsApp to ask what is in, or visit Shop D39 on the third floor.

Final Thoughts

Swiss rope-making roots explain a lot about Mammut: trim cuts made for movement, hoods that stay put in wind, and packs that sit comfortably on the hips. For Kenyan hikers, the brand makes the most sense as a hardshell for the rains, a fleece for cold starts and a daypack for long days, ideally bought thrifted in good condition.
